name: Cool (reflective) roof
cooling_evidence: London model: about -1.2 C average 2 m air temperature, up to about -2 C locally, on the two hottest days of 2018. Vienna model: about -0.25 C (roof albedo up to 0.45) to -0.5 C (up to 0.7) in dense areas.
source: Brousse et al. 2024, Geophysical Research Letters, doi:10.1029/2024GL109634; Zuvela-Aloise et al. 2018, Theoretical and Applied Climatology, doi:10.1007/s00704-016-2024-2

name: Street trees
cooling_evidence: Review of 200+ studies: average -3.8 C (SD 3.1) air temperature reduction, so very variable. London city-scale model: only about -0.3 C on average for street-level vegetation. Local effects are much larger than city-wide effects.
source: GCARE review (Univ. of Surrey), The Innovation 2024, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2666675824000262; Brousse et al. 2024, Geophysical Research Letters, doi:10.1029/2024GL109634

name: Green wall
cooling_evidence: Review of 200+ studies: average -4.1 C (SD 4.2) air temperature reduction, very variable across studies.
source: GCARE review (Univ. of Surrey), The Innovation 2024, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2666675824000262

name: Green roof
cooling_evidence: London model: about 0 C on average city-wide, but a daytime cooling effect. Vienna model: heat load reduction of similar size to high-reflectivity roofs, but only about 45% of roof area is suitable and the potential is mostly in industrial areas on the outskirts.
source: Brousse et al. 2024, Geophysical Research Letters, doi:10.1029/2024GL109634; Zuvela-Aloise et al. 2018, Theoretical and Applied Climatology, doi:10.1007/s00704-016-2024-2

name: Reflective pavement
cooling_evidence: Multi-criteria scoring study (literature and expert judgement, not measured temperatures): reflective pavements 2.45 vs street trees 3.50 overall, but better on thermal comfort and applicability. Higher albedo can raise radiant load on pedestrians.
source: Janusaite and Mikucioniene 2026, Mokslas - Lietuvos ateitis, doi:10.3846/mla.2026.27186

name: Unsealing paved surfaces
cooling_evidence: Tested as a scenario (reduction of paved surfaces) in Vienna NbS modelling; no figures used here.
source: Modelling the efficiency of Nature-based Solutions to decrease extreme heat in dense urban areas in Vienna, Urban Climate, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2212095525002962 (confirm this is the full paper)

name: Pocket park
cooling_evidence: Parks: average -3.2 C in the review as reported in the press (check the paper for the spread). Small green spaces cool much less: one reviewed study found up to about 0.3 C over 40 m for 0.5 to 2 ha.
source: GCARE review (Univ. of Surrey), The Innovation 2024, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2666675824000262; press summary at ribaj.com

name: Green corridor
cooling_evidence: No dedicated evidence found; rationale is extending the cooling of parks and river corridors.
